summary: Olympic National Forest lookout site: a 1937 L-4 cab or a 1943 R-6 ground house, removed or destroyed in 1968. Sources disagree on design; Willhite reports cable posts still anchored.

facts.design: Disputed: L-4 cab built 1937 (Register, firelookout.com) or a wood 14-by-14 standard R-6 plan ground house built 1943 (Forest Service inventory, as quoted by Forest Lookouts and Willhite)
facts.status_note: Lookout gone. Cab removed or destroyed in 1968 (sources differ on which); Willhite reports cable posts still anchored at the summit

access.note: No closure or permit is mentioned in the two accounts; the route is an overgrown former road and a steep, sparsely marked climb

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give an L-4 cab built in 1937. Willhite says use likely began in 1937 and that the cab seems to have been built in 1943; he quotes a Forest Service structural inventory that lists a 1943 wood 14x14 standard R-6 ground house, which Forest Lookouts also cites. The story gives both dates and does not choose.
Register and Forest Lookouts say removed in 1968; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1968. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Design and build year are disputed. The Register (and firelookout.com) describe an L-4 cab built 1937 and removed or destroyed 1968. Forest Lookouts and Willhite quote a Forest Service structural inventory for a 1943 14x14 standard R-6 ground house, which may be the structure the brief calls R-6. The brief's R-6 design is therefore not proposed as a correction; the editor should choose a wording for the record. Brief elevation 1023.5 m matches the Register's 3,358 ft (1,024 m). Access 'unknown' in the brief could be updated to public from the two accounts, but no closure or permit was found, and nothing here encourages climbing; WTA and Willhite describe an unmaintained route. The 1964 season and the 1944 newspaper note are secondary quotes via Forest Lookouts and were not checked against the newspaper archive. Verification 2026-10-09: the story no longer treats the 1943 cab and the 1943 ground house as one building; it reports the Willhite date and the inventory separately. 'Aircraft Warning Service' and 'wartime' are not on the Forest Lookouts page (it says only 'AWS' and gives 1942 dates), so the story uses neither. The 1942 Chriswell date is the memoir's 1942 entry (the memoir spans 1933 to 1971). 'The hike is rough' was dropped: Willhite calls the old road section a very nice trail and says the climb is steep at times. Neither Willhite nor the WTA 2018 trip report mentions a closure or permit (checked against full page text).
